outputs.block:7:text:0: IN MEMORIAM . One of India’s most celebrated artists, Jogen Chowdhury, died in Kolkata at 87, reports The New Indian Express . He had been ill with a rare type of blood cancer, according to his family. Trained at the Government College of Art & Craft from 1955 to 1960 and later at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts in Paris in the 1960s, he was among a second generation of postcolonial artists who reshaped contemporary art in India. “Chowdhury’s rich contributions in the field of art are evident in numerous government buildings … The works he left behind will remain for centuries,” said West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Known for his figurative expressionist works, often using a cross-hatching technique to distort the human body, Chowdhury blended Western modern artistic currents with local Indian influences. In the 1960s and 1970s, “many of our major artists were fond of doing abstract art, thinking that it was ‘Modern’ and the ultimate expression of art,” Chowdhury told The Punch Magazine in late 2020.
